premises.statement: A finite actualization instance can be described by a subject, respect, potential state, actual state, and an actualizer.
The source distinguishes actuality and potentiality in the same respect from different respects.
The source posits ordered efficient causes and rejects self-causation on the ground that a cause would then be prior to itself.
The third way reasons from generation/corruption and modal possibility to necessary being.
The fourth way reasons from degrees to maximality and from maximality to causation of perfections.
The fifth way describes regular operation toward ends in unintelligent natural bodies and infers intelligent direction.
The objection cites evil; the reply asserts that good can be brought from permitted evil.
The objection assigns natural events to nature and deliberate acts to human reason/will; the reply cites higher direction and a first principle.
The sed contra cites Exodus “I am who am.”
The source rejects a cause being prior to itself.
For this finite profile, an efficient-cause edge is mapped to a prior_to relation so that the source-order rationale can be exposed as a conditional conflict witness.

obligations.statement: The objection infers that an infinite good would exclude all evil, while evil is observed.
obligations.reason: Source inference and reply are inventoried; the theological permission-and-good-making response is not established by the finite causal fragments.

obligations.statement: The objection claims natural events reduce to nature and deliberate acts to human reason or will, so no divine posit is needed.
obligations.reason: The objection is recorded as a source argument; adequacy of those explanations is not decided by this model.

obligations.statement: The sed contra cites Exodus “I am who am” as an authority for the conclusion.
obligations.reason: Scriptural authority is recorded separately and is not converted into an independently verified ontological fact.

obligations.statement: One thing cannot simultaneously be mover and moved in the same respect, while it may differ by respect.
obligations.reason: The exact same-aspect impossibility principle is not independently derivable in the runtime; the model only scopes a finite witness by aspect.

obligations.statement: An essentially ordered chain of movers cannot regress infinitely and therefore has a first unmoved mover.
obligations.reason: Unbounded regress cannot be represented or proven here; a finite chain with a stipulated unmoved root is only a conditional witness, not proof of universal termination.

obligations.statement: Nothing is an efficient cause of itself because it would have to be prior to itself.
obligations.reason: The source-order principle and efficient-cause-to-priority rule produce a BOTH-valued prior_to(x,x) conflict when self-causation is supplied. That conditional contradiction witness does not prove the self-cause input false or discharge the source claim.

obligations.statement: In an ordered efficient-cause chain, absence of a first cause would remove intermediate and ultimate effects; infinite regress is impossible.
obligations.reason: Unbounded regress and universal first-cause necessity are outside the finite runtime evidence.

obligations.statement: Generated and corrupted things are possible to be and not be; not all beings are merely possible.
obligations.reason: The third Way depends on temporal modal quantification from possibility of nonexistence to a necessary being; that inference cannot be run in this finite profile.

obligations.statement: If all beings were possible not to be, there would have been a time with nothing; nothing would begin without something existing, contrary to present existence.
obligations.reason: Temporal modal quantification and the transition from possible nonexistence to an all-absent time are not expressible without an unbounded/modal engine.

obligations.statement: A necessary being without a cause of its necessity is required, and is the cause of necessity in others.
obligations.reason: The per-se necessity and causal closure steps are not independently established by this profile.

obligations.statement: Degrees of goodness, truth, and nobility imply a maximum in each relevant order.
obligations.reason: The maximality inference over qualitative degrees is unsupported by available finite predicates.

obligations.statement: What is maximal in a genus causes the properties of that genus; a maximally true/good/noble being causes being, goodness, and perfection in others.
obligations.reason: The maximality-to-causation bridge is a substantive philosophical premise, not a runtime theorem.
